# Interview: P01

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** Catherine Scovini is responsible for quality assurance and regulatory affairs at Eurosets. She is the primary contact for certification activity with TUV SUD.
- **Workflow:** She initiates requests by email or phone, gathers internal information before contacting the auditor, maintains Appendix ABC in Excel, manages change/review cycles, and tracks project modules in a personal Excel database.
- **Goal:** Maintain accurate product and certification data while completing certification activities and financial closure predictably.
- **Emotions and stance:** She describes Appendix ABC maintenance as "very tough," revision realignment as "uncomfortable," and billing closure as troublesome. She sees a shared digital platform as useful when it supports updates, process timing, and a portfolio-level overview.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "We start with the request by mail and then we send that to our auditor, lead auditor an application or change a notification and we complete all the documentation that she requests."
Code: #code/email-led-service-request

> "Actually we manage it with an Excel file file in our server and when they wrote it or depending on the project on the application request ask us to freeze the appendix."
Code: #code/versioned-excel-master-data

> "We create a subsequent revision of this appendix to manage the add of additional information going through time until the next freezing request from TUV SUD."
Code: #code/versioned-excel-master-data

> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "It is very tough because we have some thousands of code and then the number of devices is very high."
Code: #code/high-volume-product-data

> "We have an ERP, but ERP doesn't manage all the information that ABC then there is the equipment and the technical documentation."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "When we freeze the appendix ABC, we create a new version within revision. Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "It's not very easy to manage this system because we can work on the file, but also TUV SUD works on the file."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Sometimes the seller, it's not possible to pass the copying code and pass the seller."
Code: #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel

> "We find some trouble in copy and paste the data from one to another file, not always being possible to edit the Excel."
Code: #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel

> "It's not clear for me when the process ends with the service cost invoice payment."
Code: #code/unclear-billing-closure

> "There are some delay in our invoice, and then our department, the account department is sometimes very in trouble for close relativity and all that."
Code: #code/unclear-billing-closure

> "Sometimes we didn't receive the support. It's a big problem because we didn't receive any answer or any support for using this kind of information."
Code: #code/unanswered-process-support

> "Personally, I maintain tracking of the approaches in an Excel file, signing the steps of the file."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "In this moment it's not work for all the project or for the whole activity."
Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "If the approaches are clear and follow all the steps of our certification project, I think it's very useful because it's a guide that helps us to fill all this information."
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "In this case, you can copy the product family information or you have to fill singularly each code?"
Code: #code/bulk-data-entry-needed

> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information."
Code: #code/bulk-data-entry-needed

> "With this kind of system we cannot have an overview and a summary of all the list of our devices with our devices with a list of all the study barrier sterilization process or main supplier."
Code: #code/portfolio-level-data-overview

> "In parallel way will be very useful to have also the system that if this information can put in a table or Excel file in order to see also the same view of appendix ABC of today."
Code: #code/portfolio-level-data-overview

> "With Daria, we are quite well informed about the information needed."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "She sends a mail with a list of information requests or a list of document requests, but she's very, very online with the request and the activity."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Theme Match

No existing theme notes were present in `02_themes` at the start of analysis. The following new themes are justified because the codes describe distinct, directly evidenced mechanisms rather than a generic dissatisfaction with the workflow:

|---|---|---|
| #code/versioned-excel-master-data; #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/high-volume-product-data; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources; #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel | [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]] | New theme: no existing theme could capture the data-maintenance mechanism. |
| #code/revision-realignment-after-review | [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]] | New theme: distinct review and version-control mechanism. |
| #code/unclear-process-timing; #code/personal-excel-process-tracking; #code/partial-platform-coverage | [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]] | New theme: distinct status and coverage mechanism. |
| #code/unclear-billing-closure; #code/unanswered-process-support | [[Unclear Commercial Closure and Support]] | New theme: distinct post-assessment/billing mechanism. |
| #code/bulk-data-entry-needed; #code/portfolio-level-data-overview; #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow | [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]] | New theme: direct future-state requirements, kept separate from current pain mechanisms. |

# Interview: P02

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** A Senior Regulatory Affairs Manager is the primary contact for certification work. She assembles technical documentation from subject-matter experts, submits it to TUV SUD, and is the sole UCI user on her side.
- **Workflow:** She submits applications through UCI, coordinates assessment scope and quotations, maintains a living Appendix ABC across MDR and MDSAP requirements, tracks projects and costs in Excel, and collaborates with TUV SUD through regular calls.
- **Goal:** Maintain accurate certification data, predict review scope and costs, and complete product changes without duplicated or error-prone administrative work.
- **Emotions and stance:** She describes Appendix ABC maintenance as a "huge effort," cost estimation as "extremely difficult," and unplanned assessment modules as a power imbalance. She values the recurring, transparent exchange with named TUV SUD contacts.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Ich hab mich dran gewöhnt, dass es nur via U.C.I. ist. Man kann gut darauf nachher referenzieren, wenn der Request mal liegen bleibt, dann schreib ich ein Mail."
>
> Translation: "I have become used to it only being via UCI. You can refer to it well afterwards; when the request is left pending, then I write an email."
Code: #code/request-follow-up-requires-email

> "Dort wissen wir ganz genau, was der Nodified Body pro Stunde verrechnet. Und dort wissen wir ganz genau, was ein Experte kostet und wie viel nachher der Experte für einen Review abgerechnet hat."
>
> Translation: "There, we know exactly what the notified body charges per hour. And we know exactly what an expert costs and how much the expert charged for a review."
Code: #code/opaque-review-costs

> "Ich kann sie natürlich defenden, weil sie teilweise einfach nicht da ist zu einem Entwicklungsprojekt."
>
> Translation: "Of course, I can defend this because it is sometimes simply not available for a development project."
Code: #code/development-data-evolves

> "Nicht mal Appendix ABC von MDSAP und MDAR sind angeglichen."
>
> Translation: "Not even Appendix ABC for MDSAP and MDR are aligned."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel, weil ich brauche es ja eh, die Revision 09 vom MDR Appendix, weil der MDSAP Appendix brauch ich parallel jedes Jahr, weil der hat noch die ganzen Ablaufdaten hinten drin."
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel because I need revision 09 of the MDR Appendix anyway; I also need the MDSAP Appendix in parallel every year because it still contains all the expiry dates."
Code: #code/certificate-expiry-tracked-in-parallel-versions

> "Ich hab mit 2 geplant oder ups, war dann wirklich oder die Unterschiede, oder?"
>
> Translation: "I planned for two, then it suddenly became something else; the differences are enormous."
Code: #code/opaque-review-costs

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg."
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."
Code: #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale

> "Das ist einfach, wo wir sicherlich ablegen, auch auch Dokumentation, zum Beispiel Deficiency Reports. Wo wir dran arbeiten können, die sind außerhalb vom DocuBridge."
>
> Translation: "That is simply where we store documentation as well, for example deficiency reports that we can work on; they are outside DocuBridge."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Das ist eine umfangreiche Excel Liste, damit wir eine Übersicht haben. Wann sind welche Review fertig? Wann beginnen sie? Wenn die Kosten umfangreicher sind und es Teilabrechnungen gibt, müssen wir das natürlich auch wissen, dass wir die Kosten tracken können."
>
> Translation: "It is a comprehensive Excel list so that we have an overview: when are which reviews finished, when do they begin? When costs are larger and there are partial invoices, we also have to know that so we can track the costs."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "Das nicht jedes Mal ändern bei jeder Application."
>
> Translation: "Not having to change it every time for every application."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Da wird persönlich individuell benannt. Ja, ja, keine Chance."
>
> Translation: "It is named personally and individually. Yes, no chance."
Code: #code/document-organization-by-service

> "Was man nicht hat, ist den Request Progress. Der finde ich sehr transparent noch."
>
> Translation: "What one does not have is the request progress. I find that very transparent."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Für mich reicht eigentlich, wenn es so ist, theoretisch bei Udemed. Und von dem her, es muss keine Machine to Machine sein. Ich denke, mit Excel hochladen ist für uns vollkommen in Ordnung."
>
> Translation: "For me, it is enough if it is theoretically like EUDAMED. It does not have to be machine-to-machine. I think uploading Excel is completely fine for us."
Code: #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity

> "Was ist, wenn sich was ändert? Ich denk, das ist das größte Thema von allem. Wie merk ich das? Denk ich auch daran, dass ich dort auch noch was ändern muss, weil das wird jetzt immer signifikant schlimmer."
>
> Translation: "What happens when something changes? I think that is the biggest issue of all. How do I notice it? Do I also remember that I have to change something there, because it is becoming significantly worse now?"
Code: #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data

> "Ich denke, der Austausch ist wirklich super, den wir haben. alle 3 Wochen auch und wir haben sehr einen guten und regen Austausch, sehr transparenten, da kann ich wirklich gar nichts sagen."
>
> Translation: "I think the exchange we have is really great, every three weeks as well. We have a very good, lively, and transparent exchange; I really cannot say anything negative about it."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/request-follow-up-requires-email; #code/personal-excel-process-tracking; #code/request-progress-visibility; #code/document-organization-by-service | [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]] | Direct confirmation: tracking and follow-up still require external tools; add P02 evidence and related pain points. |
| #code/development-data-evolves; #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity; #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data | [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]] | Direct confirmation: data must be staged, reusable, connected, and maintained as it changes. |
| #code/misaligned-appendix-structures; #code/certificate-expiry-tracked-in-parallel-versions; #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources | [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]] | Direct confirmation: parallel structures and sources increase manual data-management burden. |
| #code/opaque-review-costs; #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale | [[Unpredictable Commercial Scoping]] | No existing theme fits the pre-quotation pricing and assessment-scope mechanism; create a new preliminary theme. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]] | Direct confirmation: regular, named contact supports transparency and should be retained. |
| #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale | [[Unclear Commercial Closure and Support]] | Related pattern only: both concern commercial engagement, but assessment scoping precedes service closure; do not increase the theme's count or confidence. |
| #code/misaligned-appendix-structures | [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]] | Related pattern only: both create version complexity, but this evidence concerns misaligned structures rather than post-review comment reconciliation. |

## Reference

# Interview: P03

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** A Quality Management System Manager and ISO 13485 management representative at Ortofix. She coordinates QMS changes, audits, and notified-body communication on quality-system matters, while Regulatory Affairs owns product-related communication.
- **Workflow:** QMS and Regulatory Affairs jointly prepare Appendix ABC from Oracle Fusion and other departmental sources; they anticipate changes in monthly calls, formalize them by email, manage evidence in SharePoint, and maintain separate Appendix ABC datasets for certification schemes and EUDAMED.
- **Goal:** Complete well-scoped changes without duplicate work, maintain accurate product and certificate information, and preserve traceable communication across personnel changes.
- **Emotions and stance:** She finds Appendix ABC difficult to maintain at the current portfolio scale, values monthly meetings highly, and describes repeated assessment or resubmission as double work.

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "We have one for the G15 for the ISO. And then we have the other for MDSAP."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "We have to fill in again all the information for all products."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "The solution of machine system that speak together will be the best solution."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "The solution that we can upload, for example, information like clinical supplier, we can upload our templates, could be a good compromise for me."
Code: #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information."
Code: #code/eudamed-data-reuse

> "Maybe a common repository could be beneficial in order to work all on the same version."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "Sometimes we submit the changes and there is a lot of time between the submission and the approval. So it's difficult because things in the company continue to move on."

# Interview: P04

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** Two Regulatory Affairs specialists at a large manufacturer act as the notified-body interface for a broad portfolio. They prepare applications, maintain Appendix ABC, coordinate with Quality Management and Sterility Assurance, and use monthly and project-specific meetings with TUV SUD.
- **Workflow:** They submit clear cases by email with Appendix ABC changes, receive a UCI case after offer acceptance, and upload technical documentation there. Internally, they extract most data from Siemens Teamcenter and SAP, maintain a SharePoint working copy, and keep a separate reference-number appendix for high-volume certificates.
- **Goal:** Maintain one valid, traceable current data state while reducing manual transcription, version reconciliation, and the risk of mistakes across certification changes.
- **Emotions and stance:** The participants say Appendix ABC versioning is "very, very difficult" and describe manual reconciliation as very laborious. They value improving UCI status information and recurring meetings with TUV contacts.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Ich glaube auch im im U.C.I. Tool sind ja die Slots mit hinterlegt. Das das hilft."
>
> Translation: "I think the slots are also stored in the UCI tool. That helps."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz."
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch."
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export."
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Die Versionierung ist sehr, sehr schwierig."
>
> Translation: "Versioning is very, very difficult."
Code: #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision

> "Mein Worst Case war, dass wir 'ne neue Version gemacht haben. Gleichzeitig kam eine von von unserer Key Accounterin plus dann kam parallel aus München noch die neue Version davon."
>
> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."
Code: #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision

> "Es ist natürlich bei, ich weiß nicht wie viel Datenpunkten, sehr, sehr, sehr mühsam, das dann manuell nachzupflegen."
>
> Translation: "With I do not know how many data points, it is of course very, very, very laborious to manually carry that forward."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Das Hin und Hergeklicke, das stimmt."
>
> Translation: "All the clicking back and forth, that is true."
Code: #code/cross-tab-data-navigation

> "Die eingeschränkten Rechte, also dass ich nicht Zeilen hinzufügen kann oder löschen kann."
>
> Translation: "The restricted permissions, meaning that I cannot add or delete rows."
Code: #code/restricted-row-editing

> "Ich reich die zwar ein, dass ich sie für mich, aber danach geht es doch immer alles nach einer TÜV-Projektliste."
>
> Translation: "I submit it so that I have it for myself, but afterwards everything proceeds according to a TUV project list."
Code: #code/customer-change-id-not-retained

> "Dann habe ich parallel eben die Arbeitsversion V24."
>
> Translation: "Then I have the working version V24 running in parallel."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Ein Portal, ein Zugang, also ein Endprodukt oder wie auch immer man es nennen will."
>
> Translation: "One portal, one access point, an end product, or whatever one wants to call it."
Code: #code/shared-certification-repository

> "Eine automatisierte Prüfung auf Validität der Daten. Vielleicht, vielleicht auch sowas wie 'n wie 'ne Erinnerungsfunktion."
>
> Translation: "An automated check of the validity of the data. Perhaps also something like a reminder function."
Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks

> "Wenn mein Supplier 'n TÜV-Süd Zertifikat habt, dass ihr euch das selber zieht. Ihr habt es schließlich auch ausgestellt."
>
> Translation: "When my supplier has a TUV SUD certificate, you should retrieve it yourselves. After all, you issued it."
Code: #code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates

> "Wir haben 'nen ungefähr 'nen monatlichen Call, wo aber dann auch Quality Sterility Assurance dabei ist, wo unsere offenen Themen besprochen werden."
>
> Translation: "We have an approximately monthly call that also includes Quality and Sterility Assurance, where our open topics are discussed."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision; #code/revision-realignment-after-review | [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]] | Direct confirmation: multiple concurrent Appendix states require manual comparison and carry-forward work. |
| #code/fragmented-product-data-sources; #code/cross-tab-data-navigation; #code/restricted-row-editing | [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]] | Direct confirmation: manual list production, navigation across dependent tabs, and fixed row structures increase error risk and effort. |
| #code/system-to-system-data-integration; #code/automated-data-validity-checks; #code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates | [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]] | Direct confirmation: data should be exchanged from a leading system, validated automatically, and reused where TUV SUD already owns the source record. |
| #code/request-progress-visibility; #code/unclear-process-timing; #code/customer-change-id-not-retained; #code/shared-certification-repository | [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]] | Direct confirmation: UCI status has improved, but certificate timing and traceability from customer change IDs through project correspondence remain insufficient. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]] | Direct confirmation: cross-functional monthly calls provide valuable proactive coordination. |
| #code/restricted-row-editing | [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]] | Related pattern only: editing restrictions contribute to version-management difficulty but are a distinct template constraint; do not increase interview count based on this code alone. |

# Interview: P05

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** Two experienced Regulatory Affairs managers at a large manufacturer manage MDR remediation, Class III device maintenance, renewals, and notified-body communication for separate operating units.
- **Workflow:** They initiate work through recurring meetings or email, submit applications and Appendix ABC updates, manage high-volume product and supplier metadata from distributed systems, and use UCI to differing degrees depending on regional onboarding and device class.
- **Goal:** Maintain correct product and supplier data, understand the certification timeline through final certification-body review, and avoid missed review actions while retaining direct working relationships with TUV contacts.
- **Emotions and stance:** They describe Excel maintenance and synchronization as a heavy manual burden. They welcome a digital system but explicitly want it to complement, not replace, personal communication.

# Interview: P06

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participants and setting:** A Director of Regulatory Affairs, a CE Regulatory Affairs team lead, and a regulatory-requirements specialist at ERBE describe how a 25-person department manages MDR and MDSAP Appendix ABC activity alongside global registrations.
- **Workflow:** The team submits most requests through UCI, maintains controlled Appendix ABC versions in its document-management system, consolidates product and supplier data from PLM, other internal systems, EUDAMED, and country-specific databases, then tracks submissions internally when UCI status is not current enough.
- **Goal:** Submit the right information once, understand what each service request requires, maintain a reliable current record, and see whether TUV has received, reviewed, or accepted the submission.
- **Emotions and stance:** Participants regard the current Excel work as costly, repetitive, and error-prone, while also reporting responsive personal support. They want contextual guidance and validation, not a long static manual or excessive notifications.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Das ist beim TÜV Süd auch 'ne Excel-Liste, wo halt aus meiner Sicht 'ne Tabellenkalkulationssoftware verwendet wurde, um 'ne Datenbank aufzubauen. Ist aus meiner Richtung nicht gut geeignet."
>
> Translation: "At TUV SUD it is also an Excel list where, from my perspective, a spreadsheet application is being used to build a database. From my perspective, it is not well suited."
Code: #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel

> "Wir haben halt auch immer so, sag ich mal, doppelt und dreifach Pflege, weil jemand muss es ja auch in die Health Canada Datenbank eintragen, dann müssen wir es noch mal in das Appendix A. B. C. eintragen und dann noch mal in unser System eintragen."
>
> Translation: "We also always have double and triple maintenance, because someone has to enter it in the Health Canada database, then we have to enter it again in Appendix ABC, and then again in our system."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Im Moment machen wir alles über das U.C.I. Portal."
>
> Translation: "At the moment, we do everything through the UCI portal."
Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen."
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren."
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Aber da hatte ich bei den Produkten schon einiges ausgefüllt gehabt, wo dann der Herr Bartholomä gesagt hat, nee, wenn ich das so und so angebe, müssen Sie die und die Prüfung machen, weil es ja so nicht richtig ist."
>
> Translation: "I had already completed quite a few product entries where Mr. Bartholomae said that if I specify it this way, you have to perform certain assessments because it is not correct that way."
Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten."
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Und deswegen sind wir dann hergegangen und haben quasi 'ne eigene Übersicht gemacht, wo wir eigentlich die gleichen Informationen nehmen und etwas detaillierter noch beschreiben, damit wir damit klarkommen und dann intern quasi auch kommunizieren können."
>
> Translation: "That is why we created our own overview, using essentially the same information but describing it in more detail so we can manage it and communicate internally."
Code: #code/personal-excel-process-tracking

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam."
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."
Code: #code/high-volume-product-data

> "Ich fänd es besser, wenn es eben nicht übers U.C.I. Portal gehen würde, sondern über 'ne definierte Schnittstelle, dass eben, ich sag mal in Realtime, ab dem Zeitpunkt, wo ich auf den Knopf drück, jetzt bitte senden, dass dann die Daten übertragen werden."
>
> Translation: "I would prefer it not to go through the UCI portal but through a defined interface, so that in real time, from the moment I press send, the data are transferred."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden."
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."
Code: #code/eudamed-data-reuse

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung."
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Wenn ich jetzt eine Neuproduktanmeldung habe, was brauchen Sie dafür noch mit dazu, reicht da nur die IFQ, wollen Sie da gleich Broschüren haben oder sonstige Informationen?"
>
> Translation: "If I have a new product registration, what else do you need for it? Is the IFQ enough, or do you also want brochures or other information?"
Code: #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen."
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."
Code: #code/request-progress-visibility

> "Ich kenn es schon aus der Vergangenheit bei anderen Unternehmen, wenn ich von den Systemen so viele Bling und Bings und hier ist was geschehen und hier ist was geschehen, dann habe ich also schon mehrfach überlegt, da gibt es so 'n Overflow und was passiert, keiner erfasst die Sachen mehr, weil es zu viel Bling, Bling und Bing und Bang ist."
>
> Translation: "I know from the past at other companies that when systems produce so many pings and notifications that something happened, there is an overflow and nobody notices things anymore because there is too much pinging."
Code: #code/critical-uci-notification-missed

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel; #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/high-volume-product-data | [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]] | Direct confirmation: Excel is treated as an unsuitable database, repeated entry spans several external and internal systems, and large lists become slow and error-prone. |
| #code/revision-realignment-after-review | [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]] | Direct confirmation: TUV-created versions must be downloaded, re-versioned, and returned to the internal controlled-document workflow. |
| #code/request-progress-visibility; #code/personal-excel-process-tracking; #code/critical-uci-notification-missed | [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]] | Direct confirmation: an outdated UCI overview leads to an internal tracker; participants need receipt/review confirmation but caution against high-volume notifications. |
| #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow; #code/system-to-system-data-integration; #code/eudamed-data-reuse; #code/automated-data-validity-checks | [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]] | Direct confirmation: a future workflow should use conditional fields, prefilled data, system interfaces, and validation rather than static forms and repeated manual entry. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]] | Direct confirmation: responsive project meetings and direct questions provide effective guidance today. |
| #code/critical-uci-notification-missed | [[Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation]] | Related evidence: the participant warns that notification overload can make important changes invisible, reinforcing the existing alert-design implication without creating a separate theme. |

# Interview: P07

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- **Participant and setting:** Tatjana Malak leads the Quality Management System team at Brainlab. Regulatory Affairs manages product-specific changes and device lists, while her team manages applications, audits, certificates, and QMS-related change notifications.
- **Workflow:** Brainlab coordinates open items and ongoing changes in a shared Excel file and triweekly calls with named TUV contacts. It maintains controlled Appendix files alongside product, supplier, and technical information held in Windchill, Polarion, SAP, EUDAMED, and national databases.
- **Goal:** Supply current structured data once, preserve controlled manufacturer records, see notified-body review outcomes, and make change, audit, certification, and budget decisions with predictable timing and rationale.
- **Emotions and stance:** The participant values the established human collaboration but describes the Appendix as the most painful source of manual work. She is open to joint digital workflows if ownership, roles, auditability, and technical interfaces are explicit.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Dieses Format hat sich in den letzten Jahren so raus entwickelt mit dieser geteilten Excelliste und den dreiwöchigen Meetings und das funktioniert mittlerweile für uns sehr gut."
>
> Translation: "This format has developed over recent years with the shared Excel list and triweekly meetings, and it now works very well for us."
Code: #code/auditor-guidance-works

> "Also es läuft aktuell sehr viel parallel zwischen E-Mail und UCI Portal."
>
> Translation: "Currently, a great deal runs in parallel between email and the UCI portal."
Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber oder alles eben was auch auf dem Appendix B. und C. ist auszutauschen."
>
> Translation: "There is currently no digital interface to exchange information about the products themselves or everything in Appendix B and C."
Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Supply-Informationen haben wir wiederum in anderen Datenbanken, das pflegen wir in S.A.P., das heißt, das müssen wir separat rausziehen."
>
> Translation: "We have supply information in other databases, maintained in SAP, which means we have to extract it separately."
Code: #code/fragmented-product-data-sources

> "Oft ist es ja so, dass wenn man 'ne Change Notification einreicht, dass zu dem Zeitpunkt die Details, die in den Appendix eingetragen werden müssen, noch nicht klar sind, auch noch nicht vonnöten sind."
>
> Translation: "When submitting a change notification, the details that must be entered in the Appendix are often not yet clear or needed at that time."
Code: #code/development-data-evolves

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History."
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."
Code: #code/shared-data-audit-trail

> "Wir haben zum Beispiel dieses Jahr im Audit erlebt, dass die Auditoren in einer Version vom Appendix A. B. C. nachgeschaut haben, die total outdated war."
>
> Translation: "This year during the audit, the auditors reviewed a version of Appendix ABC that was completely outdated."
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?"
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"
Code: #code/unclear-process-timing

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen."
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."
Code: #code/misaligned-appendix-structures

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind."
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist."
>
> Translation: "We then had to manually find out what information William had entered so we could transfer it into our working files and not lose it the next time we submitted the file."
Code: #code/revision-realignment-after-review

> "Also das ist natürlich extrem unpraktisch."
>
> Translation: "That is, of course, extremely impractical."
Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?"
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"
Code: #code/opaque-review-costs

> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird und wie groß unsere Rechte sozusagen sind, da direkt was zu pflegen, möglicherweise sollte es noch sowas wie 'ne Admin oder eine quasi eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die die grundlegenderen Approvals macht."
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data are maintained and how extensive our direct editing rights are, there may need to be an admin or higher-level role that makes more fundamental approvals."
Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "Was da drin steht, gehört zu uns."
>
> Translation: "What is in it belongs to us."
Code: #code/role-based-data-governance

> "In der Datenbank könnte ich mir ja gut vorstellen, dass man das über Status abfangen kann. Also Entered by Manufacturer, Reviewed by Notified Body, Feedback by Notified Body oder so."
>
> Translation: "In a database, I could imagine handling this through statuses: entered by manufacturer, reviewed by notified body, feedback by notified body, or similar."
Code: #code/shared-data-audit-trail

## Theme Match

| Code | Theme match | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance; #code/fragmented-product-data-sources; #code/misaligned-appendix-structures | [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]] | Direct confirmation: separate controlled files and distributed source systems require repeated manual maintenance and reconciliation. |
| #code/revision-realignment-after-review; #code/shared-data-audit-trail | [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]] | Direct confirmation: reviewer changes must be manually transferred back into a controlled customer record because the shared process has no audit trail or field-level review states. |
| #code/partial-platform-coverage; #code/unclear-process-timing | [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]] | Direct confirmation: UCI and email run in parallel, and audit submission timing is unclear enough that auditors can use an outdated Appendix version. |
| #code/system-to-system-data-integration; #code/development-data-evolves; #code/role-based-data-governance | [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]] | Direct confirmation: data become available at different stages and a future interface needs structured exchange with scoped contributor, reviewer, and approver roles. |
| #code/auditor-guidance-works | [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]] | Direct confirmation: triweekly shared-topic meetings with named contacts are an effective current working pattern. |
| #code/opaque-review-costs | [[Unpredictable Commercial Scoping]] | Direct confirmation: unexplained cost increases undermine budget planning and require repeated follow-up for rationale. |

## Reference
Analysis followed [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Steps 1-4. New P07 codes are registered in [[Global Tags]].

# Interview: P08

## Context
- **Participants:** Yvonne Kuba and Lisa Ketterer (Quality Management and Audit Management), Rainer Sieglinger (Regulatory Affairs authority manager), and Susan Schirmer (Regulatory Affairs Labeling and Data Management) at Esculap AG.
- **Workflow:** The group submits service requests through UCI, coordinates certification projects, and maintains a high-volume Appendix ABC spreadsheet on a manufacturer-controlled SharePoint site.
- **Goal:** Keep certification data current with less manual effort while preserving manufacturer ownership, meaningful validation, and direct human clarification for ambiguous cases.
- **Observed sentiment:** Participants welcomed UCI improvements and a future data-based solution, but described spreadsheet revisioning, cross-functional data collection, and field interpretation as labor-intensive and error-prone.

## Transcript in Meaning Units

> "Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio."
>
> Translation: "It is a very manual task to maintain this huge table with a great deal of information that we as the manufacturer have to provide, and we do not have a small product portfolio."
>
> Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance, #code/high-volume-product-data

> "Mit U.C.I. hat sich schon einiges verbessert, weil man da tatsächlich ja elektronisch diese Anträge stellen kann, dann auch zu diesen Projekten dann immer alles an einer Stelle in der Kommunikation und auch von den Projektdokumenten her hat."
>
> Translation: "UCI has already improved quite a lot because applications can be submitted electronically and the communication and project documents are then all in one place for those projects."
>
> Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage

> "Wenn das Projekt angelegt wurde, ich sehe die Antragsunterlagen nicht mehr in U.C.I."
>
> Translation: "When the project has been created, I can no longer see the application documents in UCI."
>
> Code: #code/request-document-continuity

> "Der Appendix A.B.C. ist momentan ein Leben, also eine Excel-Tabelle, die wir auf einem externen SharePoint, auf den auch quasi unsere TÜV-Ansprechpartner Zugriff haben, abgelegt haben und dort pflegen."
>
> Translation: "Appendix ABC currently has its own life as an Excel table that we store and maintain on an external SharePoint site, to which our TUV contacts have access."
>
> Code: #code/partial-platform-coverage, #code/versioned-excel-master-data

> "Unter den Versionswechseln habe ich manchmal gelitten, ne. Also wenn man da noch 'ne Spalte eingeführt hat oder sowas und aufgefordert war, da noch was und doch noch was zu verändern oder oder sowas."
>
> Translation: "I have sometimes suffered under version changes, for example when another column was introduced and we were asked to change one thing and then another."
>
> Code: #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision

> "Wir haben uns mit Hilfe von Farben kenntlich gemacht, wenn wir sagen, okay, die und die Artikel könnten jetzt eigentlich ausgelöscht werden, weil wir selber nicht löschen können."
>
> Translation: "We used colours to mark the articles that could now actually be deleted because we cannot delete them ourselves."
>
> Code: #code/restricted-row-editing

> "Komplex machen es erstmal die ganz vielen Arbeitsmappen, das ist schon mal komplex, die unterschiedlichsten Informationen, die quasi seitens der benannten Stelle aus unserer Sicht erforderlich sind."
>
> Translation: "What makes it complex first of all are the many worksheets and the very different kinds of information that, from our perspective, the notified body requires."
>
> Code: #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance, #code/cross-tab-data-navigation

> "Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank auf unserer Seite die Daten und pack die da einfach rein in 'ner bestimmten Art und Weise."
>
> Translation: "We cannot simply press a button and tell it to take the data from a particular database on our side and put it into the table in a particular way."
>
> Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Dann kommt es ganz oft mit Hashtag Wert Ausrufezeichen und wir wissen halt auch nicht, was haben wir jetzt da falsch gemacht oder ist da jetzt, also es verunsichert halt einfach 'n bisschen."
>
> Translation: "It often then shows hashtag value exclamation mark, and we do not know what we have done wrong; it is simply a bit unsettling."
>
> Code: #code/automated-data-validity-checks

> "Ich hab in der Vergangenheit halt öfters Probleme mit, wie komme ich von meiner oder wie kriege ich die Daten von meiner Quelle in ihr Ziel, wenn da so 'ne starre Maske ist."
>
> Translation: "In the past, I have often had problems getting data from my source into its destination when there is such a rigid form."
>
> Code: #code/system-to-system-data-integration

> "Wir sind schon etwas über 50 Prozent glaube ich, aber alle haben wir noch nicht drin."
>
> Translation: "I think we are a little over 50 percent, but we do not have everything in there yet."

# Theme: Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness

## Definition
Responsive, named auditor guidance helps the participant understand information and document requirements before and during certification activity.

## Associated Codes
- #code/auditor-guidance-works

## Representative Quotes
> "With Daria, we are quite well informed about the information needed." - P01

> "She sends a mail with a list of information requests or a list of document requests, but she's very, very online with the request and the activity." - P01

> "Ich denke, der Austausch ist wirklich super, den wir haben. alle 3 Wochen auch und wir haben sehr einen guten und regen Austausch, sehr transparenten, da kann ich wirklich gar nichts sagen." - P02
>
> Translation: "I think the exchange we have is really great, every three weeks as well. We have a very good, lively, and transparent exchange; I really cannot say anything negative about it."

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "We have a weekly meeting with our project handler and coordinator." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung." - P06
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."

> "Dieses Format hat sich in den letzten Jahren so raus entwickelt mit dieser geteilten Excelliste und den dreiwöchigen Meetings und das funktioniert mittlerweile für uns sehr gut." - P07
>
> Translation: "This format has developed over recent years with the shared Excel list and triweekly meetings, and it now works very well for us."

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 also reports occasional unanswered requests for support, which may concern a different support channel or topic. P02, P03, P05, P06, and P07 positive assessments depend on regular named-contact meetings and may not generalize to customers without this arrangement. P05 also reports that system-only alerts can be missed, while P06 warns that over-notification can obscure important events.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains High: P07 provides a seventh direct confirmation that recurring named-contact communication is valuable, particularly as a complement to digital notifications. Test whether structured in-product guidance can preserve this tailored support without reducing access to a human contact.

## Linked Pain Points
None. This theme documents a working pattern.

## Linked Insights
No insight yet: only one interview supports this preliminary theme.

# Theme: Change Assessment Cannot Keep Pace with Internal Change

## Definition
Internal changes continue while notified-body assessment is pending, and incomplete cross-functional impact assessment can require resubmission. Both mechanisms create rework, delayed implementation, and reliance on expedited processing.

## Associated Codes
- #code/change-progresses-during-assessment
- #code/incomplete-change-impact-assessment
- #code/cross-functional-change-impact-gaps

## Representative Quotes
> "Sometimes we submit the changes and there is a lot of time between the submission and the approval. So it's difficult because things in the company continue to move on." - P03

> "If we submit documentation and we discover only later that we didn't do an assessment, we need to resubmit again the document. So it's double work for us, for the notified body." - P03

## Contradicting Evidence
P03 reports that monthly meetings help clarify borderline changes before formal communication. This reduces uncertainty but does not remove the internal coordination and assessment-timing issues.

## Open Questions
Does the same pattern recur across manufacturers, and would shared change status, cross-functional impact checklists, or earlier assessment estimates most reduce rework?

## Linked Pain Points
- [[Change Assessment Lags Internal Change Progress]]
- [[Incomplete Change Impact Assessment Causes Resubmission]]

## Linked Insights
No insight yet: only one interview supports this preliminary theme.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Theme: Concurrent Revision Reconciliation

## Definition
When Appendix ABC is frozen for review while the customer continues work in a new revision, later reviewer comments must be manually reconciled into the active version.

## Associated Codes
- #code/revision-realignment-after-review
- #code/concurrent-appendix-version-collision
- #code/shared-data-audit-trail

## Representative Quotes
> "When we freeze the appendix ABC, we create a new version within revision. Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "It's not very easy to manage this system because we can work on the file, but also TUV SUD works on the file." - P01

> "Mein Worst Case war, dass wir 'ne neue Version gemacht haben. Gleichzeitig kam eine von von unserer Key Accounterin plus dann kam parallel aus München noch die neue Version davon." - P04
>
> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."

> "Es ist natürlich bei, ich weiß nicht wie viel Datenpunkten, sehr, sehr, sehr mühsam, das dann manuell nachzupflegen." - P04
>
> Translation: "With I do not know how many data points, it is of course very, very, very laborious to manually carry that forward."

> "Then they would kind of maintain like the most up-to-date versions on their end. So that part's a bit confusing to me, I suppose." - P05

> "We also have tech doc reviews going on where we're being asked to change the appendices from that. So we've got multiple sources asking for changes at the same time." - P05

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

P02 reports that MDR and MDSAP Appendix structures are not aligned. This creates related version complexity, but it is distinct from reconciling active revisions and concurrent incoming changes.

Confidence remains High: P08 provides a sixth direct confirmation and shows that both recurring template changes and responsibility for version migration create reconciliation burden. # Theme: Limited End-to-End Process Visibility

## Definition
Certification stakeholders understand major phases but lack reliable timing and cross-project visibility, leading them to maintain independent tracking and seek a platform that covers the complete workflow.

## Associated Codes
- #code/unclear-process-timing
- #code/personal-excel-process-tracking
- #code/partial-platform-coverage
- #code/request-follow-up-requires-email
- #code/request-progress-visibility
- #code/document-organization-by-service
- #code/shared-certification-repository
- #code/customer-change-id-not-retained
- #code/certification-body-status-black-box
- #code/critical-uci-notification-missed

## Representative Quotes
> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear." - P01

> "Personally, I maintain tracking of the approaches in an Excel file, signing the steps of the file." - P01

> "Das ist eine umfangreiche Excel Liste, damit wir eine Übersicht haben. Wann sind welche Review fertig? Wann beginnen sie?" - P02
>
> Translation: "It is a comprehensive Excel list so that we have an overview: when are which reviews finished, and when do they begin?"

> "Was man nicht hat, ist den Request Progress." - P02
>
> Translation: "What one does not have is the request progress."

> "Maybe a common repository could be beneficial in order to work all on the same version." - P03

> "Most of the communication are managed via mail. And sometimes it's easy to lost the mail and lost the traceability." - P03

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."

> "Die sehe ich nie wieder, weder auf der Rechnung noch auf der Rückmeldung." - P04
>
> Translation: "I never see it again, neither on the invoice nor on the feedback."

> "As soon as it goes to the CERT body, then we kind of lose all visibility to what's going on." - P05

> "We were like a week or two late in realizing that we had questions." - P05

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten." - P06
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

> "Also es läuft aktuell sehr viel parallel zwischen E-Mail und UCI Portal." - P07
>
> Translation: "Currently, a great deal runs in parallel between email and the UCI portal."

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?" - P07
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"

> "Mit U.C.I. hat sich schon einiges verbessert, weil man da tatsächlich ja elektronisch diese Anträge stellen kann, dann auch zu diesen Projekten dann immer alles an einer Stelle in der Kommunikation und auch von den Projektdokumenten her hat." - P08
>
> Translation: "UCI has already improved quite a lot because applications can be submitted electronically and the communication and project documents are then all in one place for those projects."

> "Wenn das Projekt angelegt wurde, ich sehe die Antragsunterlagen nicht mehr in U.C.I." - P08
>
> Translation: "When the project has been created, I can no longer see the application documents in UCI."

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 says the main phases are clear and can obtain information requirements from the lead auditor. P02 considers the overall process transparent and values regular contact. P03 also says the process is clear with notified-body support. P04 says UCI slots and response notifications have improved status visibility. P05 reports that UCI notification behavior can be inconsistent and that the certification-body step remains opaque. P06 says the UCI overview is a good start but is not current enough, and wants explicit receipt or review acknowledgement. P07 values UCI for project documents but still relies on email and asks for explicit audit-submission timing. P08 values UCI's project-level communication and documents but cannot retrieve the application documents after project creation. The remaining gap is final certificate timing, action-required alerts, in-context follow-up, document visibility, acknowledgement, and traceability from internal change IDs into the TUV process.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains High: P08 provides an eighth direct confirmation, adding the requirement that submitted request documents remain accessible once the project exists. Test which dates, owners, status transitions, document groupings, ID mappings, acknowledgement states, audit deadlines, and alert escalation rules would be actionable enough to replace personal tracking.

- [[Digital Platform Does Not Cover All Projects]]
- [[Request Follow-up Requires External Email]]
- [[Documents Are Not Grouped by Service]]
- [[Customer Change IDs Disappear Across TUV Process]]
- [[Critical UCI Notifications Can Be Missed]]

## Linked Insights
No insight yet: only one interview supports this preliminary theme.

# Theme: Manual Appendix ABC Data Management

## Definition
Maintaining Appendix ABC requires manual, ongoing consolidation of a high-volume device portfolio from fragmented internal sources. Excel cannot reliably support the reuse and update work required.

## Associated Codes
- #code/versioned-excel-master-data
- #code/high-effort-appendix-maintenance
- #code/high-volume-product-data
- #code/fragmented-product-data-sources
- #code/copy-paste-limits-in-excel
- #code/misaligned-appendix-structures
- #code/certificate-expiry-tracked-in-parallel-versions
- #code/cross-tab-data-navigation
- #code/restricted-row-editing
- #code/supplier-certificate-data-fragmentation

## Representative Quotes
> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated." - P01

> "We find some trouble in copy and paste the data from one to another file, not always being possible to edit the Excel." - P01

> "Nicht mal Appendix ABC von MDSAP und MDAR sind angeglichen." - P02
>
> Translation: "Not even Appendix ABC for MDSAP and MDR are aligned."

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel, weil ich brauche es ja eh, die Revision 09 vom MDR Appendix, weil der MDSAP Appendix brauch ich parallel jedes Jahr, weil der hat noch die ganzen Ablaufdaten hinten drin." - P02
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel because I need revision 09 of the MDR Appendix anyway; I also need the MDSAP Appendix in parallel every year because it still contains all the expiry dates."

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "We have to fill in again all the information for all products." - P03

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch." - P04
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."

> "Das Hin und Hergeklicke, das stimmt." - P04
>
> Translation: "All the clicking back and forth, that is true."

> "So now we're having to go back through now and do a complete assessment of the 10,000 CFNs and ensure that you know everything is accurate." - P05

> "The one that comes to mind most prominently is probably Appendix C for the suppliers." - P05

> "Das ist beim TÜV Süd auch 'ne Excel-Liste, wo halt aus meiner Sicht 'ne Tabellenkalkulationssoftware verwendet wurde, um 'ne Datenbank aufzubauen. Ist aus meiner Richtung nicht gut geeignet." - P06
>
> Translation: "At TUV SUD it is also an Excel list where, from my perspective, a spreadsheet application is being used to build a database. From my perspective, it is not well suited."

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam." - P06
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen." - P07
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind." - P07
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."

> "Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio." - P08
>
> Translation: "It is a very manual task to maintain this huge table with a great deal of information that we as the manufacturer have to provide, and we do not have a small product portfolio."

> "Komplex machen es erstmal die ganz vielen Arbeitsmappen, das ist schon mal komplex, die unterschiedlichsten Informationen, die quasi seitens der benannten Stelle aus unserer Sicht erforderlich sind." - P08
>
> Translation: "What makes it complex first of all are the many worksheets and the very different kinds of information that, from our perspective, the notified body requires."

> "Wenn dann sich mal was in der Produktfamilie zum Beispiel in A. 3 ändert, dann denkt man vielleicht nicht dran, nach vorne zu springen. Es ist menschlich." - P08
>
> Translation: "If something changes in the product family, for example in A.3, people may not think to jump back to the front. It is human."

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 considers Appendix ABC important as a summary of device technical specifications; P02 values a living version that supports coordination; P03 says a small, certificate-specific site list could remain separate; P04 uses it as a required certification artifact but not as the primary working basis for discussions. P05 sees the metadata itself as manageable but identifies supplier and high-volume maintenance as especially vulnerable to source-to-source errors. P06 values the data purpose but reports that the spreadsheet becomes slow at scale. P07 needs the data for certification but reports manual maintenance across multiple certificate-specific files and fragile links among A, B, and C. P08 sees the data as necessary but reports many worksheets, multiple source systems, and cross-tab dependencies. The problem is the manual, duplicated maintenance burden, not the purpose of the data.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains High: P08 provides an eighth direct confirmation, including a large portfolio, many worksheets, and cross-tab dependencies that people can miss during routine updates. Test which supplier certificate and site fields can be sourced or verified automatically and which authorized record edits require audit controls.

# Theme: Scalable Structured Data Collaboration

## Definition
A future digital workflow must accept data at the project stage where it is known, support bulk reuse for large portfolios, and retain a cross-portfolio overview for customer and reviewer collaboration.

## Associated Codes
- #code/guided-end-to-end-workflow
- #code/bulk-data-entry-needed
- #code/portfolio-level-data-overview
- #code/development-data-evolves
- #code/bulk-upload-with-relationship-continuity
- #code/change-reminder-for-distributed-data
- #code/system-to-system-data-integration
- #code/eudamed-data-reuse
- #code/automated-data-validity-checks
- #code/reuse-issued-supplier-certificates
- #code/certification-process-performance-metrics
- #code/role-based-data-governance

## Representative Quotes
> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information." - P01

> "In parallel way will be very useful to have also the system that if this information can put in a table or Excel file in order to see also the same view of appendix ABC of today." - P01

> "Für mich reicht eigentlich, wenn es so ist, theoretisch bei Udemed. Und von dem her, es muss keine Machine to Machine sein. Ich denke, mit Excel hochladen ist für uns vollkommen in Ordnung." - P02
>
> Translation: "For me, it is enough if it is theoretically like EUDAMED. It does not have to be machine-to-machine. I think uploading Excel is completely fine for us."

> "Was ist, wenn sich was ändert? Ich denk, das ist das größte Thema von allem. Wie merk ich das?" - P02
>
> Translation: "What happens when something changes? I think that is the biggest issue of all. How do I notice it?"

> "The solution of machine system that speak together will be the best solution." - P03

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information." - P03

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export." - P04
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."

> "Eine automatisierte Prüfung auf Validität der Daten. Vielleicht, vielleicht auch sowas wie 'n wie 'ne Erinnerungsfunktion." - P04
>
> Translation: "An automated check of the validity of the data. Perhaps also something like a reminder function."

> "We have that metadata within, you know, our own systems." - P05

> "We always welcome more metrics, so I think that would be extremely helpful for us as we're not only planning projects, but that also kind of take a look internally on what can we do if we need to resource." - P05

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden." - P06
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."

> "Ideal wäre es, wenn ich halt sage, ich möchte jetzt das tun, es gibt den Fall, den Fall, den Fall und dann werde ich durch diesen Prozess durchgeführt, welche Felder muss ich wie ausfüllen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Ideally, I would say what I want to do, there are these cases, and then I am guided through the process: which fields do I need to fill in and how?"

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber oder alles eben was auch auf dem Appendix B. und C. ist auszutauschen." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is currently no digital interface to exchange information about the products themselves or everything in Appendix B and C."

> "Je nachdem, was dann alles an Daten gepflegt wird und wie groß unsere Rechte sozusagen sind, da direkt was zu pflegen, möglicherweise sollte es noch sowas wie 'ne Admin oder eine quasi eine höher gestellte Rolle geben, die die grundlegenderen Approvals macht." - P07
>
> Translation: "Depending on what data are maintained and how extensive our direct editing rights are, there may need to be an admin or higher-level role that makes more fundamental approvals."

> "Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank auf unserer Seite die Daten und pack die da einfach rein in 'ner bestimmten Art und Weise." - P08
>
> Translation: "We cannot simply press a button and tell it to take the data from a particular database on our side and put it into the table in a particular way."

> "Dann kommt es ganz oft mit Hashtag Wert Ausrufezeichen und wir wissen halt auch nicht, was haben wir jetzt da falsch gemacht oder ist da jetzt, also es verunsichert halt einfach 'n bisschen." - P08
>
> Translation: "It often then shows hashtag value exclamation mark, and we do not know what we have done wrong; it is simply a bit unsettling."

> "Also ich würd es, glaub ich, nicht begrüßen, wenn sie eigenständig ändern. Also ich glaub, es sollte schon irgendwie immer in Rücksprache mit uns erfolgen." - P08
>
> Translation: "I do not think I would welcome it if you changed things independently. I think it should always happen in consultation with us."

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 considers some initial project information easy to provide, but says supplier and manufacturing information can be premature for early-stage or phased submissions. P02 prefers Excel upload over a machine-to-machine interface, while P03 and P04 identify system-to-system exchange as ideal and template upload as a practical compromise. P05 needs a system that can coexist with internal metadata sources and expose planning metrics. P06 has mature product data but needs a mixture of EUDAMED reuse, other-source enrichment, and guided input. P07 requires a controllable interface from multiple internal systems and distinct contributor, reviewer, and approver rights. P08 wants data transfer from manufacturer systems, but validation that warns rather than independently overwrites manufacturer data. An API is valuable when the customer has a sufficiently structured leading system, not a universal prerequisite.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains High: P08 adds an eighth direct confirmation of reusable structured data and makes non-destructive validation an explicit requirement. Test which integrations, imports, certificate lookups, guided workflows, and reports can preserve data ownership and auditability.

## Linked Pain Points
No current-state pain point is linked yet; this is a future-state requirement theme.

## Linked Insights
- [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]]
- [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]]

# Theme: Unclear Commercial Closure and Support

## Definition
After technical work concludes, unclear service completion, invoice timing, and occasional unavailable support make financial and administrative closure difficult.

## Associated Codes
- #code/unclear-billing-closure
- #code/unanswered-process-support

## Representative Quotes
> "It's not clear for me when the process ends with the service cost invoice payment." - P01

> "There are some delay in our invoice, and then our department, the account department is sometimes very in trouble for close relativity and all that." - P01

## Contradicting Evidence
P01 has named contacts for technical matters; the reported support gap concerns obtaining answers about this information, not the absence of every relationship.

## Related Evidence
P02 reports unclear pre-quotation costs and assessment-module rationale. This is related commercial evidence but concerns commercial scoping before service acceptance, rather than closure or support; interview count and confidence are unchanged.

## Open Questions
Are late invoices an isolated operational issue or a predictable consequence of unclear completion criteria?

## Linked Pain Points
- [[Unclear Invoice Timing Delays Administrative Closure]]

## Linked Insights
No insight yet: only one interview supports this preliminary theme.

# Theme: Unpredictable Commercial Scoping

## Definition
Before a quotation is accepted, the customer cannot reliably understand review-cost components or why assessment modules are included. The uncertain scope makes budget estimation and challenge of the proposed assessment difficult.

## Associated Codes
- #code/opaque-review-costs
- #code/unclear-assessment-module-rationale

## Representative Quotes
> "Und dort wissen wir ganz genau, was ein Experte kostet und wie viel nachher der Experte für einen Review abgerechnet hat." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we know exactly what an expert costs and how much the expert charged for a review."

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?" - P07
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

## Contradicting Evidence
P02 understands which certification service to request; the uncertainty concerns cost and assessment-module scope, not basic service selection. P07 also needs routine-cost estimates but reports that explanations arrive only after repeated follow-up.

## Open Questions
Confidence remains Medium: P07 provides a second direct cross-company confirmation that costs can arrive without sufficient rationale for budget planning. Test which explanation, cost breakdown, and forecast would be sufficient for customers to predict and challenge scope before quotation acceptance.

## Linked Pain Points
- [[Opaque Cost and Assessment Scope]]

## Linked Insights
No insight yet: only one interview supports this preliminary theme.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Pain Point Register

Last consolidated: 2026-07-17. All thirteen pre-existing pain points were reviewed after P07; no duplicate underlying mechanisms were found. PP02 concerns reconciling concurrent reviewer, template, and customer revisions, while PP13 concerns missed inbound action notifications. PP09 concerns assessment timing after a complete submission, while PP10 concerns omitted internal impact assessment before or after submission, so they remain distinct. # Pain Point: Change Assessment Lags Internal Change Progress

**Theme:** [[Change Assessment Cannot Keep Pace with Internal Change]]
**Description:** Internal work continues while a submitted change awaits notified-body approval, so later changes may no longer match the submitted documentation.
**Trigger:** A change assessment has a long interval between submission and approval.
**Impact:** Implementation may be postponed, documentation becomes stale, and the company may need to use expedited assessment.
**Workaround:** Plan changes earlier and use monthly meetings or an expedited process when timing becomes critical.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 2
**Interview IDs:** P03

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Sometimes we submit the changes and there is a lot of time between the submission and the approval. So it's difficult because things in the company continue to move on." - P03

> "We try to plan as much as possible all the changes, but sometimes it's not possible and we need to use the expedite process." - P03

## Possible Opportunity
Test shared assessment states, expected approval dates, and a mechanism to flag related internal changes before the submitted package becomes outdated.

# Pain Point: Critical UCI Notifications Can Be Missed

**Description:** Deficiency questions can arrive in UCI without a reliable accompanying personal email, and high notification volume can cause the system alert to be overlooked.

## Possible Opportunity
Test a configurable, high-salience alert for action-required deficiencies, with clear acknowledgement and escalation states rather than increasing general notification volume.
