notes.body:
# Pain Point: High-Effort Appendix ABC Maintenance

**Theme:** [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]]
**Description:** Keeping Appendix ABC current is labor-intensive for a large, dynamically changing device portfolio.
**Trigger:** New or changing devices and codes require updates to the Appendix ABC file.
**Impact:** Significant recurring manual effort to maintain certification data.
**Workaround:** Maintain the file in Excel and create successive revisions after freezes.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 14
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06, P07, P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "The appendix ABC, it's quite impenitive. Very tough. Very tough. Because it's a collection of more information on our devices and we have to keep it already updated." - P01

> "It is very tough because we have some thousands of code and then the number of devices is very high." - P01

> "Das ist ein Riesenaufwand schon." - P02
>
> Translation: "That alone is a huge effort."

> "Ich pflege Revision 09 von eurem Ding parallel." - P02
>
> Translation: "I maintain revision 09 of your document in parallel."

> "The Appendix ABC is really difficult to be maintained." - P03

> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "Daraus füttern wir und leider auch mit einem hohen manuellen Aufwand dann einfach die Listen nur für euch." - P04
>
> Translation: "We feed the lists for you from that, unfortunately with a high manual effort."

> "So now we're having to go back through now and do a complete assessment of the 10,000 CFNs and ensure that you know everything is accurate." - P05

> "The one that comes to mind most prominently is probably Appendix C for the suppliers." - P05

> "Wir haben halt auch immer so, sag ich mal, doppelt und dreifach Pflege, weil jemand muss es ja auch in die Health Canada Datenbank eintragen, dann müssen wir es noch mal in das Appendix A. B. C. eintragen und dann noch mal in unser System eintragen." - P06
>
> Translation: "We also always have double and triple maintenance, because someone has to enter it in the Health Canada database, then we have to enter it again in Appendix ABC, and then again in our system."

> "Wenn man da nicht einen leistungsfähigen Rechner hat, wird es sehr, sehr langsam." - P06
>
> Translation: "If you do not have a high-performance computer, it becomes very, very slow."

> "Vor allem haben wir ja aktuell mehrere Excel-Dateien, die wir pflegen müssen." - P07
>
> Translation: "Above all, we currently have several Excel files that we have to maintain."

> "Das ist natürlich eine total händische Arbeit, am Ende sicherzustellen, dass diese Verknüpfungen zwischen den A, B und C nach wie vor gültig sind." - P07
>
> Translation: "It is completely manual work to ensure in the end that the links between A, B, and C are still valid."

> "Es ist eine sehr manuelle Aufgabe, diese riesen Tabelle zu pflegen mit ganz vielen Informationen, die wir als Hersteller bereitstellen müssen und sollen. Und wir haben auch nicht gerade ein kleines Produktportfolio." - P08
>
> Translation: "It is a very manual task to maintain this huge table with a great deal of information that we as the manufacturer have to provide, and we do not have a small product portfolio."

## Possible Opportunity
Test bulk update and reuse mechanisms that preserve Appendix ABC's function as a technical-data summary.

# Pain Point: Incomplete Change Impact Assessment Causes Resubmission

**Theme:** [[Change Assessment Cannot Keep Pace with Internal Change]]
**Description:** Change coordinators can omit affected departments or assessments, and the gap is found only after submission or during implementation planning.
**Trigger:** A cross-functional change is assessed without all affected departments and activities being included from the start.
**Impact:** The change must be revised, implementation can be postponed, and the customer and notified body repeat work.
**Workaround:** Transfer change coordination to QMS and use monthly meetings to clarify borderline changes before formal submission.

**Representative Quotes:**
> "The mistakes happen mostly due to communication. Because sometimes during a project, for example, during a change, some departments are not included." - P03

## Possible Opportunity
Test a change-impact workflow that makes affected functions, required assessments, and notified-body implications explicit before submission.

# Pain Point: Opaque Cost and Assessment Scope

**Theme:** [[Unpredictable Commercial Scoping]]
**Description:** The customer cannot see a clear cost breakdown for reviews or reliably predict and contest assessment modules included in a quotation.
**Trigger:** Estimating a new certification, change, or annual routine cost before committing budget.
**Impact:** Cost estimates can change substantially, making budget planning unreliable and leaving the customer unable to influence assessment scope.
**Workaround:** Ask repeatedly for rationale and either accept the quoted scope or delay the work.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 4
**Interview IDs:** P02, P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Und da haben wir auch keinen Durchblick in den Kosten, was da zusammenkommt." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we have no visibility into the costs that add up there."

> "Ich kann es dann akzeptieren oder nicht? Da habe ich als Hersteller gar keine Macht." - P02
>
> Translation: "I can then accept it or not? As a manufacturer, I have no power at all."

> "Und 2 haben wir wirklich versucht, weg zu argumentieren mit rationalen und wir bekamen sie nicht weg." - P02
>
> Translation: "And we really tried to argue two of them away with rationales, but we could not get rid of them."

> "Meistens kommen die kommentarlos, dann fragen wir nach, hoppla, das ist 30% mehr als letztes Jahr. Woher kommt die Erhöhung, könnt ihr uns das bitte erklären?" - P07
>
> Translation: "They usually arrive without comment, then we ask: this is 30% more than last year. Where does the increase come from? Could you please explain it?"

Test an itemized pre-quotation breakdown that links each assessment module to the change rationale and shows the cost effect.

# Pain Point: Reviewer Feedback Requires Revision Realignment

**Theme:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]]
**Description:** Reviewer comments, template changes, and customer working copies can create concurrent Appendix ABC states that require manual realignment into the active version.
**Trigger:** TUV SUD reviews or updates an Appendix while the customer continues work, or a revised template arrives alongside a customer revision.
**Impact:** Rework and risk of inconsistent data across customer and reviewer versions.
**Workaround:** Re-update the active revision after comments arrive and maintain an internal sequence of submitted and working versions.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 10
**Interview IDs:** P01, P04, P05, P06, P07, P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "It's not very easy to manage this system because we can work on the file, but also TUV SUD works on the file." - P01

> "Die Versionierung ist sehr, sehr schwierig." - P04
>
> Translation: "Versioning is very, very difficult."

> "Dann habe ich parallel eben die Arbeitsversion V24." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I have the working version V24 running in parallel."

> "Then they would kind of maintain like the most up-to-date versions on their end. So that part's a bit confusing to me, I suppose." - P05

> "We also have tech doc reviews going on where we're being asked to change the appendices from that. So we've got multiple sources asking for changes at the same time." - P05

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Dann mussten wir aber wieder händisch rausfinden, welche Informationen hat der William eingetragen, damit wir dann unsere Arbeitsdateien übertragen können, damit wir beim nächsten Mal, wenn wir das schicken, seine Information nicht verloren ist." - P07
>
> Translation: "We then had to manually find out what information William had entered so we could transfer it into our working files and not lose it the next time we submitted the file."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

## Possible Opportunity
Test shared revision states, review comments linked to a record, and explicit reconciliation flows.

notes.title: Unclear Certification Step Timing
notes.body:
# Pain Point: Unclear Certification Step Timing

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Description:** The participant understands the major certification phases but cannot reliably see timing or the current status from one step to the next.
**Trigger:** Managing an active certification request across departments and project types.
**Impact:** Uncertainty about progress, expected certificate timing, and whether TUV has received or reviewed a submission.
**Workaround:** Personally track project steps in Excel and ask the auditor.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 8
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P04, P05, P06, P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Sometimes, personally, it's not too clear timing from step to step, but the main phases are quite clear." - P01

> "Das ist eine umfangreiche Excel Liste, damit wir eine Übersicht haben. Wann sind welche Review fertig? Wann beginnen sie?" - P02
>
> Translation: "It is a comprehensive Excel list so that we have an overview: when are which reviews finished, and when do they begin?"

> "Dann weiß ich aber halt nicht, krieg ich nach einer Woche oder nach 7 Monaten mein Zertifikat. Da da herrscht noch große Intransparenz." - P04
>
> Translation: "Then I still do not know whether I will receive my certificate after one week or after seven months. There is still major lack of transparency there."

> "As soon as it goes to the CERT body, then we kind of lose all visibility to what's going on." - P05

> "Die Übersicht auf dem U.C.I. Portal ist 'n guter Anfang, ja, aber es ist durchaus ausbaufähig, um das halt transparenter und aktueller zu gestalten." - P06
>
> Translation: "The overview in the UCI portal is a good start, but it can definitely be expanded to make it more transparent and up to date."

> "Ja, 'ne Statusmeldung, dass eben die Eintragungen, die wir vorgenommen haben, auch vom TÜV angeschaut worden sind und dass 'ne grüne Lampe angeht, zum Beispiel zu sagen, ja, vielen Dank, haben wir gesehen." - P06
>
> Translation: "Yes, a status message that the entries we made have also been viewed by TUV, and that a green light comes on, for example to say: yes, thank you, we have seen it."

> "Wir haben zum Beispiel dieses Jahr im Audit erlebt, dass die Auditoren in einer Version vom Appendix A. B. C. nachgeschaut haben, die total outdated war." - P07
>
> Translation: "This year during the audit, the auditors reviewed a version of Appendix ABC that was completely outdated."

> "Das heißt, das wäre zum Beispiel so 'ne Sache: Sollen wir als Hersteller einfach proaktiv X Wochen vorm Audit 'ne neue Version einreichen, sollen wir warten, bis wir gefragt werden?" - P07
>
> Translation: "That would be one issue: should we as a manufacturer proactively submit a new version X weeks before an audit, or should we wait until we are asked?"

## Possible Opportunity
Validate which status changes and forecast dates would be useful and reliable enough to display.

# Insight: Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source

**Insight:** The burden of Appendix ABC is not its certification purpose but maintaining overlapping product data manually across internal systems, multiple Appendix structures, and EUDAMED. Customers need a reusable structured source that carries shared product data forward while preserving certificate-specific relationships and fields.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]]

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> "In any case, we need to take all the information one by one and update it manually." - P03

> "If there is a possibility to create a link between information available in Eudamed and information available here, that can help us to easily fill out the information." - P03

> "It's very tough to enter Eudamed one ref to one ref and repeat this information." - P01

> "Wenn ihr uns 'ne Datenbankschnittstelle mit den mit den Werten gebt, dann definieren wir die bei uns und dann kriegt ihr die per Export." - P04
>
> Translation: "If you provide us with a database interface for the values, then we define them on our side and you receive them by export."

> "We have that metadata within, you know, our own systems." - P05

> "I think if there's a better system for keeping things maintained and avoiding unintentional changes that then cause some synchronization issues, that would be preferable too." - P05

> "Wenn man so das Appendix ABC als Datenbanken machen könnte, dann können die sich erstmal aus der EuDamed bedienen, weil da sind ja die Daten vorhanden." - P06
>
> Translation: "If Appendix ABC could be made into databases, they could first draw from EUDAMED because the data are available there."

> "Es gibt aber natürlich bisher keine digitale Schnittstelle, um Informationen zu den Produkten selber oder alles eben was auch auf dem Appendix B. und C. ist auszutauschen." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is currently no digital interface to exchange information about the products themselves or everything in Appendix B and C."

> "Wir können jetzt nicht auf Knopfdruck sagen, zieh dir jetzt aus der und der Datenbank auf unserer Seite die Daten und pack die da einfach rein in 'ner bestimmten Art und Weise." - P08
>
> Translation: "We cannot simply press a button and tell it to take the data from a particular database on our side and put it into the table in a particular way."

**Business Impact:** Manual, duplicated data maintenance consumes regulatory and quality capacity and increases the chance of inconsistent certification records. P04, P05, P06, P07, and P08 show that a customer with structured leading systems still incurs this cost when TUV inputs must be manually assembled into a separate list or synchronized across changing sources.
**Design Implication:** Treat certification data as reusable structured records with imports or integrations, rather than as independently maintained spreadsheet copies. Prefill fields from EUDAMED where they overlap, then guide users through the remaining certificate-specific data. Support both system-to-system integration for mature data environments and bulk import for others, with validation that identifies incomplete or incompatible data before submission.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Insight: Digital Visibility Needs Human Escalation

**Insight:** Self-service certification visibility is valuable only when action-required events are reliably surfaced and paired with a reachable human escalation path. Status tools reduce routine follow-up, but missed system-only deficiency alerts and opaque final certification-body review can delay work unless personal communication remains available.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]], [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]]

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> "We were like a week or two late in realizing that we had questions." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "Ich kenn es schon aus der Vergangenheit bei anderen Unternehmen, wenn ich von den Systemen so viele Bling und Bings und hier ist was geschehen und hier ist was geschehen, dann habe ich also schon mehrfach überlegt, da gibt es so 'n Overflow und was passiert, keiner erfasst die Sachen mehr, weil es zu viel Bling, Bling und Bing und Bang ist." - P06
>
> Translation: "I know from the past at other companies that when systems produce so many pings and notifications that something happened, there is an overflow and nobody notices things anymore because there is too much pinging."

**Business Impact:** Delayed awareness of questions can extend review timelines, while unnecessary status-chasing consumes both customer and TUV capacity. P06 shows that indiscriminate notifications can also hide the actions users need to see.
**Design Implication:** Provide a status workspace with high-salience, acknowledged alerts for required action, and retain project-linked contact and escalation routes for questions that need judgement. Suppress routine change noise through configurable notification preferences and summaries.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Insight: Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle

**Insight:** Reusable certification data alone will not remove rework if manufacturer working copies, notified-body feedback, and template revisions evolve independently. Shared records need a controlled lifecycle that makes each party's role, review status, feedback, and field-level changes visible without allowing one party to silently overwrite another's accountable record.
**Supporting Themes:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]], [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]]

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> "When we freeze the appendix ABC, we create a new version within revision. Afterwards, we receive in some weeks or a few days, it depends, a feedback of the file with the comments of TUV SUD, and we have to re-update our updating version." - P01

> "Mein Worst Case war, dass wir 'ne neue Version gemacht haben. Gleichzeitig kam eine von von unserer Key Accounterin plus dann kam parallel aus München noch die neue Version davon." - P04
>
> Translation: "My worst case was that we created a new version. At the same time, one came from our Key Account Manager, and then a new version of it arrived in parallel from Munich."

> "Wenn dann vom TÜV was ergänzt wird oder was geändert wird, dann macht er ja eher eine neue Version. Das heißt, diese Version muss ich dann wieder runterladen und bei uns dann im Dokumentenmanagementsystem wieder versionieren." - P06
>
> Translation: "When TUV adds or changes something, it tends to create a new version. That means I then have to download that version again and version it in our document-management system."

> "Es gibt ja in dem Sinne keinen Audit Trail oder so, also wo man sieht, wer hat an 'nem Dokument was geändert, sondern es gibt ja nur diese manuell gepflegte Version History." - P07
>
> Translation: "There is no audit trail showing who changed what in a document; there is only the manually maintained version history."

> "Vielleicht noch ergänzend, eben wenn wir 'ne Versionierung haben, das war eigentlich immer ganz charmant, wenn das der TÜV dann übernommen hat, weil beim letzten Mal mussten wir es selber machen und Nein, also auf keinen Fall, das ist zu viel Aufwand." - P08
>
> Translation: "To add, when we have versioning, it was always quite nice when TUV handled it, because the last time we had to do it ourselves and, no, absolutely not, it is too much effort."

**Business Impact:** Manual reconciliation consumes regulatory and quality capacity, can lose reviewer feedback between versions, and creates inconsistent certification records even when the source product data itself is correct.
**Design Implication:** Model review as a permissioned state workflow on shared records: manufacturer entries and releases, notified-body review and feedback, explicit ownership, non-destructive validation, field-level provenance, and a visible path to resolve and approve changes.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the analysis process.

# Positive Pattern: Responsive Auditor Guidance

**Theme:** [[Auditor Guidance Supports Information Readiness]]
**Process Phase:** Request/Application; Change; Review
**Description:** Named notified-body contacts provide document lists and recurring meetings that clarify requirements before and during certification activity.
**Why it works:** Participants know whom to contact, receive actionable information requests, and can resolve borderline questions before formal submission.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** A digital workflow could remove valuable tailored guidance if it offers only static forms or generic help.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 9
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06, P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "With Daria, we are quite well informed about the information needed." - P01

> "She sends a mail with a list of information requests or a list of document requests, but she's very, very online with the request and the activity." - P01

> "Ich denke, der Austausch ist wirklich super, den wir haben. alle 3 Wochen auch und wir haben sehr einen guten und regen Austausch, sehr transparenten, da kann ich wirklich gar nichts sagen." - P02
>
> Translation: "I think the exchange we have is really great, every three weeks as well. We have a very good, lively, and transparent exchange; I really cannot say anything negative about it."

> "The best thing are the monthly meeting because I really to clarify any doubts and also to maintain the communication." - P03

> "Wir haben 'nen ungefähr 'nen monatlichen Call, wo aber dann auch Quality Sterility Assurance dabei ist, wo unsere offenen Themen besprochen werden." - P04
>
> Translation: "We have an approximately monthly call that also includes Quality and Sterility Assurance, where our open topics are discussed."

> "We have a weekly meeting with our project handler and coordinator." - P05

> "Having the personal touch is still, you know, I think it's important too." - P05

> "Positiv erwähnen möchte ich mal, der Service ist super. Also über die Projektgespräche oder wenn wir Fragen haben, wir kriegen echt sehr, sehr schnell Rückmeldung." - P06
>
> Translation: "I would like to mention positively that the service is great. Through project meetings or when we have questions, we get a response really, really quickly."

> "Dieses Format hat sich in den letzten Jahren so raus entwickelt mit dieser geteilten Excelliste und den dreiwöchigen Meetings und das funktioniert mittlerweile für uns sehr gut." - P07
>
> Translation: "This format has developed over recent years with the shared Excel list and triweekly meetings, and it now works very well for us."

# Positive Pattern: UCI Centralizes Active Project Work

**Theme:** [[Limited End-to-End Process Visibility]]
**Process Phase:** Request/Application; Review
**Description:** UCI centralizes electronic requests, project communication, and active-project documents for this participant group.
**Why it works:** Stakeholders can use a common project location instead of relying only on email recipients and individual inboxes.
**Risk if removed/redesigned away:** A redesigned workflow could lose the existing project-level communication and document context while addressing gaps in request-to-project continuity.

## Evidence
**Evidence Count:** 1
**Interview IDs:** P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Mit U.C.I. hat sich schon einiges verbessert, weil man da tatsächlich ja elektronisch diese Anträge stellen kann, dann auch zu diesen Projekten dann immer alles an einer Stelle in der Kommunikation und auch von den Projektdokumenten her hat." - P08
>
> Translation: "UCI has already improved quite a lot because applications can be submitted electronically and the communication and project documents are then all in one place for those projects."

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 6b.

# Persona: Regulatory Certification Lead

**Segment:** Regulatory certification lead at a medical-device manufacturer
**Based on Interviews:** [[P01]], [[P02]], [[P04]], [[P05]], [[P06]]

## Context
Owns or coordinates certification submissions with the notified body, consolidates technical and product data from internal systems and subject-matter experts, and maintains the Appendix ABC evidence needed for active changes and audits. Uses email, meetings, spreadsheets, and internal product-data systems to keep certification work moving.

P05 confirms that this role may manage MDR remediation, Class III maintenance, and renewals across high-volume portfolios, while using direct contact to supplement partial platform visibility.

P06 confirms that Regulatory Affairs leaders own controlled Appendix ABC versions, coordinate data from PLM and other sources, and translate team-level status into management-level reporting.

- Submit complete, traceable certification changes without repeated data entry or reconciliation.
- Maintain a reliable current state across internal product data, Appendix ABC, EUDAMED, and notified-body work.

# Recommendation: Make Review Feedback a Traceable Permissioned Workflow

**Recommendation:** Replace exchanged review-file versions with shared certification records that preserve manufacturer ownership and provide explicit statuses for manufacturer entry, notified-body review, feedback, resolution, and approval. Record field-level changes and comments, restrict actions by contributor, reviewer, and approver roles, and require customer confirmation before material reviewer-proposed changes become part of the manufacturer-controlled record.
**Evidence - Anchor Insight:** [[Shared Certification Data Needs a Controlled Review Lifecycle]]
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Concurrent Revision Reconciliation]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]], [[Reviewer Feedback Requires Revision Realignment]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce manual comparison and re-entry, prevent loss of reviewer feedback, and make the accountable current state clear to both parties.
**Risk:** The state model and permissions must distinguish material certification changes from low-risk corrections so the workflow does not introduce unnecessary approvals or bureaucracy.

## Reference

# Recommendation: Pair Action Alerts with Human Escalation

**Recommendation:** In the certification-status workspace, distinguish action-required deficiencies from routine updates, require acknowledgement and escalation for unaddressed actions, and keep a project-linked route to the responsible TUV contact. notes.title: Use Reusable Structured Certification Data
notes.body:
# Recommendation: Use Reusable Structured Certification Data

**Recommendation:** Build certificate-specific views from reusable structured product records, beginning with bulk import and prefill from EUDAMED where fields overlap. Guide users through the remaining certificate-specific fields and offer a documented system-to-system export or integration path for customers with a structured leading system. Preserve the relationships among devices, sites, suppliers, and certification schemes so customers update shared data once rather than maintain parallel Appendix ABC files.
**Evidence - Anchor Insight:** [[Certification Data Needs One Reusable Source]]
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[Manual Appendix ABC Data Management]], [[Scalable Structured Data Collaboration]], [[High-Effort Appendix ABC Maintenance]]
**Expected Effect:** Reduce recurring manual updates, duplicate entry, and data inconsistency across certification records.
**Risk:** EUDAMED does not contain every certificate-specific field, and mapping quality, access, and ownership must be validated before treating it as an authoritative source.

## Reference

| P01 | Regulatory and quality assurance lead at a medical-device manufacturer | Primary contact with the certification body; manages a large, changing device portfolio; relies on Excel, ERP, technical documentation, and auditor guidance. |
| P02 | Regulatory Affairs Manager at a medical-device manufacturer | Primary certification contact and sole UCI user; consolidates technical documentation from subject-matter experts; maintains live Appendix ABC data and project/cost tracking in Excel. |
| P03 | Quality Management System Manager at a medical-device manufacturer | ISO 13485 management representative; owns QMS changes, audits, and quality-system communication; jointly maintains Appendix ABC with Regulatory Affairs. |
| P04 | Regulatory Affairs specialists at a large medical-device manufacturer | Coordinate notified-body applications and Appendix ABC across a large product portfolio; rely on SAP, Teamcenter, SharePoint, and cross-functional coordination. |
| P05 | Regulatory Affairs managers at a large medical-device manufacturer | Manage MDR remediation, Class III maintenance, renewals, and high-volume Appendix ABC data; rely on project-handler relationships, email, and partially adopted UCI workflows. |
| P06 | Regulatory Affairs leaders at a medical-device manufacturer | Manage MDR and MDSAP Appendix ABC records across global registrations; coordinate controlled document versions, PLM and external data, UCI submissions, and management-level project reporting. |
| P07 | Quality Management System lead at a medical-device manufacturer | Manages QMS applications, audits, certificates, and QMS changes; coordinates with Regulatory Affairs on controlled Appendix records, multiple data systems, and notified-body review. |
| P08 | Cross-functional certification stakeholders at a large medical-device manufacturer | Includes Quality Management, Audit Management, Regulatory Affairs authority management, and Regulatory Affairs labeling/data management; collectively maintain high-volume Appendix ABC data and coordinate UCI projects. |

A proto-persona has been created: [[Regulatory Certification Lead]], now supported by P01, P02, P04, P05, and P06. Persona splitting check: P07 confirms a second QMS-specific participant whose audit, certificate, and QMS-change responsibilities differ from product-specific Regulatory Affairs ownership. Do not merge this role into the Regulatory Certification Lead persona; wait for one more comparable QMS interview before creating a separate persona. P08 is a mixed-role group interview, so it is recorded as evidence of cross-functional collaboration but is not counted as homogeneous support for either persona.
